newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday and traders said that sharp falls in the domestic A share markets had affected most of the repo rates.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract dived to 4.00 percent from 17.10 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover fell sharply to 7.53 million lots from 13.09 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The falls of domestic A share markets made demand for funds shrink, which hit most repo rates," one trader said. The A market in Shanghai fell 5.51 percent and Shenzhen 4.84 percent.
Traders expect rates for the three-day contract to rally next week after today's sharp losses.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market ended mostly up due to a technical rebound. The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 116.46 yuan from 116.09 yuan on Thursday.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell to 940,293 lots from 1.08 million.
"In the long run, spot rates are likely to go up, because some think the market has fallen too far, especially the 10-year bond," one trader said.
